subject.title: [BUG]: Browser tool: `snapshot` returns page content before scroll, ignoring viewport position

question: Should browser `snapshot` default to a whole-page structural read with added scroll metadata, or should OpenClaw add or make default a visible-viewport-scoped snapshot after scroll?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the documented contract does not currently promise viewport-scoped snapshots and changing the default affects model-facing browser semantics across Playwright, CDP fallback, and Chrome MCP.

options.title: Add explicit viewport-aware mode
options.body: Introduce a viewport-scoped snapshot mode or scroll/viewport metadata first, keep the current full-tree path available, and choose the default after live proof.

options.title: Change default to visible viewport
options.body: Make snapshot output match the current viewport after scroll and provide an explicit full/raw escape hatch for broad-page workflows.

options.title: Document full-tree behavior
options.body: Keep current snapshot semantics and document that agents should use labels, screenshots, or selector-scoped snapshots when viewport evidence matters.

recommendation.title: Add explicit viewport-aware mode
recommendation.body: Introduce a viewport-scoped snapshot mode or scroll/viewport metadata first, keep the current full-tree path available, and choose the default after live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current snapshot route and helper history make this the strongest routing candidate for the browser snapshot contract choice.
